3. The defendant Nos. 2-3, 5 and 12 con-tested the suit by filing 4 sets of separate written statement and the defendant No.1 did not contest the suit. According to defendant Nos. 2-3, 5 and 12 the suit land measuring 59 decimals in C.S. khatian no.183 corresponding to S.A. khatian No. 164 belonged to Sarat Chandra who during his life time transferred his entire suit land measuring 59 acres to his son Ramesh Chandra by a oral pattan and delivered possession to him. On 15.10.1946 said Ramesh Chandra sold 311/4 decimals of land out of total measuring 59 acres of land to Arefa Khatun and Sheikh Abdus Sabur by way of registered sale deed and thereafter he transferred the rest of 283/4 decimal of land to Arefa Khatun and Nazrul Haque by way of another registered sale deed dated 20.06.1960 and it may be mentioned that in the deed dated 15.10.1946 said Sarat Chandra himself put his signature as one of the attesting witness. Thereafter Arefa Khatun while owning and possession the said land transferred a portion of the suit land in favour of Abdus Sabur and Nazrul Haque and again transferred the some portion of land to Sheikh Hossain Ali and also to Ayesha Khatun and Mullick Mofazzal Hossain through defendant kabalas. Nazrul Haque sold a portion of his share to Mullick Montaz Uddin by way of registered sale deed dated 22.10.1975 and also sold the rest portion to Sheikh Hossain All and Mullick Ibrahim. Thereafter Hossain All sold his land to Saera begum by registered kabala dated 31.08.1976 and Montaz Uddin sold his share to Sara Khatun by another kabala dated 03.09.1975. Ayesha Khatun sold his purchased. land to Md. Abu Jafar by a kabala deed dated 31.08.1975, Mullick Mafazzal Hossain sold his purchased land to Abu Jafar and the said Abu Jafar thereafter sold the same to defendant No. 3 by registered kabala dated 02.07.1985. Sara Khatun sold her purchase land to defendant No. 2 and thereafter defendant Nos. 2 and 3 after purchase owning and possessing the .26 decimals of land from the northern portion of the disputed dags by constructing Golpata Sheds and the compromise decree passed in Title Suit No. 143 of 1987 was valid and the plaintiff file this false suit which is 'liable to be dismissed with cost. 

 4. Mr. Nurul Islalm Bhuiyan, learned Advocate-on-Record, appearing for the petitioners submitted that defendant No.1 Mullick Mostazabul Haque is the benamdar of the plaintiff Rabeya Khatun and the plaintiff is in possession of the Suit land since 23.10.1962 and that she acquired good title by adverse possession in the suit land on the basis of contract for sale dated 23.10.1962 with Narayan Chandra as well as on the basis of ex-parte decree dated 03.06.1969 in Title Suit No. 811 of 1969 and that present defendant No. 1 having filed Title Suit No. 143 of 1987 for ejecting the present plaintiff and others, and that suit having been decreed on 02.05.1989 on compromise with other defendants and the present plaintiff being defendant No. 10 in that suit was kept outside the compromise and she remained' in possession of the suit land, the finding by the judge of the High Court Division, that her possession in the suit land is immaterial since she is nothing but a tenant under defendant No. 1, is contrary to the materials on records in as much as defendant No. 1 did not contest the instant Suit, Appeal and Revision; that the learned appellate Court below having found that Sarat Chandra gave pattan orally to his one son Ramesh Chandra the whole suit land area 59 decimal has not been proved by evidence and that only a recital in the subsequent deed dated 15.10.1946 is not sufficient to prove such oral settlement and that Sarat Chandra the alleged attesting witness is the father of Ramesh Chandra the whole suit land area .59 decimal has not been proved by evidence and that only a recital in the subsequent deed dated 15.10.1946 is not sufficient to prove such oral settlement and that Sarat Chandra the alleged attesting witness is the father of Ramesh Chandra also has not been proved satisfactorily and that the deed by Ramesh Chandra in favour of Arefa Khatun and Nazrul Haque and the deed dated 15.10.1946 and all the deeds of 1975, 1976 and 1985 have not been legally proved and marked exhibits in the Case and having allowed the appeal decreeing the suit, the learned Judge of the High Court Division erred in making the Rule absolute without at all considering those findings of the appellate Court; that the defendant No. 1 Mullick Mostazabul Haque is the Bahagani Jamai of the plain-tiff who is also Benamder of the plaintiff and that though in the suit he filed written 'statement but did not contest the Suit at the time of .hearing and hence by admitting the plaintiffs case of acquiring title by adverse possession in the suit land and that plaintiff Rabeya Khatun is a tenant under defendant No. 1 which is not the case of the defendant No. 2 and 3; that the certified copy of the deed dated 20.06.1960 was not genuine one; that the learned Appellate. Court below having found that the deeds of the defendant No. 2 and 3 dated 31.08.1975, 03,09,1975, 02,03,1975 and 02,07,1985 and the deeds of their vendors were not legally proved and marked as exhibits and having allowed the appeal, that the plaintiff Title Suit No. 811 of 1969 was filed for kabala against Narayari Chandra having died, his full brother Ramesh Chandra was substituted as defendant and .that suit having been decreed ex-parte on 0106.1969 and subsequently Execution Case No. 9 of the 1971 was filed against said Ramesh Chandra which ended in dismissal for want of necessary affidavit and the plain-. tiff petitioners having been in continuous possession of the suit land, and the High Court Division also having found the plaintiff in possession of the suit land, ought to have held that plaintiff acquired good title by adverse possession and erred in making the Rule absolute holding that the plaintiff in possession of the suit land as tenant of defendant No. 1, though no document or rent receipt or evidence showing the plaintiff as tenant under the defendant has been produced.
